speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. Since you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress, I need to ask: Is there a family history of genetic disorders, and were there any complications during your birth or delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the preterm status and respiratory distress, have you noticed any cyanosis, grunting, or nasal flaring, and was there a need for immediate resuscitation or ventilation at birth? Also, did you notice any feeding difficulties or apnea episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas_AND_Chest_XRAY. REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide the Chest X-Ray showing the lung fields, heart size, and diaphragm position. We need to rule out severe pneumonia, TTN, or pulmonary hypoplasia immediately.
